key_insight: Generation quality for video diffusion transformers depends less on overall sparsity and more on how well the sparse attention mask aligns with the tile-wise geometry of full attention. Distilling dense attention into geometry-aware sparse masks preserves quality at high sparsity.
problem_solved: Reduces the quadratic cost of self-attention for high-resolution, long video generation while avoiding quality degradation from naively applied sparse attention.
method: Analyze the relationship between sparse mask patterns and full-attention tile geometry; show alignment — not sparsity ratio — drives quality.
Formulate tile selection as an explicit, learnable selection objective and distill dense (teacher) attention into compact, geometry-aligned sparse masks.
Integrate the distilled sparse attention into diffusion transformers to scale generation to higher resolutions and longer temporal horizons without losing visual fidelity.
impact: Allows practitioners to train and run video diffusion models more efficiently (lower memory/compute) while keeping generation quality, enabling higher-resolution and longer-duration video synthesis on realistic hardware budgets.
visual_elements: Side-by-side heatmaps: full attention vs misaligned sparse mask vs geometry-aligned sparse mask showing quality differences

paper_title: Veda: Scalable Video Diffusion via Distilled Sparse Attention
